How to use the Mortgage Calculator

  1. Enter the home price, your down payment percentage and the interest rate you were quoted.
  2. Pick the loan term and fill in property tax, insurance and any HOA dues.
  3. If you put down less than 20%, set your PMI rate (typically 0.3–1.5% per year).
  4. Review your total monthly payment and the amortization table.

Frequently asked questions

How is the monthly mortgage payment calculated?

Principal and interest use the standard amortization formula M = L·r / (1 − (1 + r)^−n), where L is the loan amount, r the monthly rate and n the number of payments. Taxes, insurance, HOA and PMI are then added.

What is PMI?

Private mortgage insurance is usually required on conventional loans with less than 20% down. It typically costs 0.3–1.5% of the loan per year and can be removed once you reach about 20% equity.

Should I choose a 15-year or 30-year mortgage?

A 15-year loan has higher monthly payments but usually a lower rate and far less total interest. A 30-year loan keeps payments lower and more flexible.

Is this an official loan quote?

No. It is an estimate for planning. Lenders will factor in your credit, fees and local taxes.
